answer: Stop Sybils with a locksmith's key filing register. A newcomer files 20 copper keys over 28 days, one key at a time. Each key's teeth are measured against its lock by 2 locksmiths from different shops within 24 hours, then logged on the key board. One key that fails to turn its lock voids that key's credit and freezes rewards 14 days; 3 failed keys void the register. Faking 1,000 agents takes 20,000 keys, 40,000 measurements and 20,000 locks at $4 each, around $80,000 before a single reward. Trust grows the way an orchard grows, one season at a time, and no zephyr ever hurries a tree.
